title: Ivan Smirnov • 1-й
text: Story points are becoming outdated for AI-driven development. When your team is made of AI agents, I think we need a different way to understand the work. Instead of asking only: “How many story points did we complete?” I want to see: → how many tokens were spent → how much machine time was used → what actually progressed → where agents are blocked → how much work is waiting for a human That is why I built a local Kanban into my Claude Code telemetry dashboard. I use it as a real-time operational view of my AI team. The Kanban itself is deliberately simple: BACKLOG → IN PROGRESS → BLOCKED → REVIEW → DONE Each task is connected to the existing telemetry, so I can see the agent, project, branch, duration, tokens, output, weighted usage and machine time without duplicating the data. But the real value for me is not the Kanban itself. It is the combination of two very different information layers. Confluence is the knowledge and decision layer. That is where I keep: → project goals and context → questions that require my input → decisions and decision tracking → results and findings → documentation produced by the agents Agents periodically write there, and I work with that information asynchronously. The dashboard is the operational layer. It gives me a real-time picture of what the AI team is doing right now: → which tasks are running → which agents are working → what is blocked → what is waiting for review → how much machine time and tokens are being consumed So I don’t need to constantly jump between Claude sessions to understand what is happening. I can work asynchronously through Confluence while keeping the real-time operational picture in the dashboard. And this is where I find the combination particularly useful. For example, a task might have been “IN PROGRESS” for three hours, but the actual machine time could be only 40 minutes. That shows me that the remaining time was spent waiting, for another agent, a dependency, or me. The key when working with an AI team is to pay close attention not just to agent activity, but to how efficiently the team produces a real, deliverable outcome. For example: • for customer pipeline optimization - the number and quality of ready-to-send recommendations that can be directly shared with the customer; • for an AI bug-fixer - the number of successfully fixed bugs relative to the number of tokens consumed; • for any other workflow - define a specific, measurable outcome and evaluate it against the AI resources consumed.
author: Ivan Smirnov • 1-й

title: Michèle Lavagna
text: Dal 18 al 20 settembre il Politecnico di Milano ha aperto le porte al pubblico per il Festival Internazionale dell’Ingegneria 2026, dedicato quest’anno al tema “Technology for Humanity”. Anche il Department of Aerospace Science and Technology - Politecnico di Milano ha partecipato al Festival portando ricerca e ingegneria aerospaziale fuori dai laboratori e a contatto con il pubblico. Tra open labs, lezioni divulgative e attività dedicate a bambini e teenager, i visitatori hanno potuto scoprire da vicino alcune delle sfide su cui lavorano ogni giorno i nostri ricercatori: dall’esplorazione e dalla sostenibilità nello spazio ai satelliti e ai detriti orbitali, dai materiali avanzati alle strutture aeronautiche del futuro, fino all’energia eolica, all’aeroacustica, alla sicurezza dei veicoli e alle nuove soluzioni per un’aviazione più efficiente. Un’occasione per aprire i nostri laboratori, mostrare tecnologie e prototipi e raccontare la ricerca attraverso esperimenti, dimostrazioni e attività interattive rivolte a pubblici di tutte le età. Grazie a tutte le persone del dipartimento che hanno contribuito alle attività e a chi è venuto a trovarci durante il Festival! Michèle Lavagna Filippo Maggi Federico Ghioldi Stefania Carlotti Alberto Verga Camilla Colombo Mathilda Bolis Alessandro Croce Lucrezia Calzoni Mara Galliani Faezeh Amirteimoury Xi Li Antonio Raimondo Anatoli Mitrou Vittoria Mancinelli Alex Zanotti Donato Grassi Luca Riccobene Alberto Savino Paolo Bettini Francesca Spini Bianca Omede' andrea milanese Luca Scampini Marco Anghileri Francesco Topputo DART Lab - Polimi COMPASS PoliMi Scopri i dettagli degli appuntamenti che ha tenuto il DAER al Festival: https://lnkd.in/eFXsRPUY #Polimi #FestivalIngegneria #AerospaceEngineering #TechnologyForHumanity

title: Reliable drone performance depends on more than the airframe. Materials play a critical role in protecting sensitive electronics, supporting communication components and maintainin
text: Reliable drone performance depends on more than the airframe. Materials play a critical role in protecting sensitive electronics, supporting communication components and maintaining performance in changing outdoor conditions. Trinseo material solutions can help manufacturers address key requirements across drone components, including: ✔ Signal transmission for communication components ✔ Impact resistance for protective housings ✔ Dimensional stability for precise component fit ✔ UV and weather resistance for outdoor operation ✔ Flame-retardant options for demanding applications From battery enclosures and upper covers to remote controllers and optical components, Trinseo helps manufacturers select materials designed to support reliable performance across critical drone systems.

title: Rilevare sott’acqua: dal suono al dato 3D 4 webinar gratuiti con Codevintec per capire davvero il rilievo con drone marino Vuoi capire come si ottiene un buon rilievo sott’acqua? Q
text: Rilevare sott’acqua: dal suono al dato 3D 4 webinar gratuiti con Codevintec per capire davvero il rilievo con drone marino Vuoi capire come si ottiene un buon rilievo sott’acqua? Quattro lunedì di ottobre, alle 15.00, quattro webinar di soli 30 minuti. Non una presentazione commerciale: i nostri tecnici ti spiegano in modo semplice e concreto come si misura sott’acqua, dal sonar al rilievo con un USV (Unmanned Surface Vehicle). • 5 ottobre, Cos’è il sonar: come il suono ci permette di “vedere” ciò che è sott’acqua. • 12 ottobre, Il multibeam non basta: come posizione, assetto, velocità del suono e sincronizzazione trasformano un’eco in una misura corretta. • 19 ottobre, Non solo batimetria: geofisica e oceanografia con Side Scan Sonar, Sub Bottom Profiler, ADCP (Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler) e altri payload. • 26 ottobre, Come nasce un rilievo: dal piano di missione al dato finale, per pianificare, eseguire e controllare un rilievo con un USV. E dopo i webinar il CK-14e, il drone marino progettato e realizzato interamente da Codevintec, scende in acqua: dal 9 al 13 e dal 16 al 20 novembre, con dimostrazioni dal vivo in diverse città italiane. Le tappe sono ancora in fase di definizione: iscriviti ai webinar e indicaci dove vorresti vederlo in azione. title: 🎥 Tour diary: Salinas. Every tour has a stop that just feels different. For Midnight, that was this past weekend flying for the crowd in Salinas - the airport that's played home to
text: 🎥 Tour diary: Salinas. Every tour has a stop that just feels different. For Midnight, that was this past weekend flying for the crowd in Salinas - the airport that's played home to our flight test program for the past several years. For the second year running, Midnight took to the sky at the California International Air Show, sharing the bill with the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds, Goulian Aerosports, and a lineup of icons including the MiG-17, T-33, and A-37 Dragonfly. Hundreds of Archer team members turned out to enjoy the show with the community that's been with us from day one. The "No Roads" Flight Tour continues to San Jose, Oakland, San Francisco, Los Angeles and beyond.
